answer.rationale: The consolidated memory_73 ('promotional pricing effective for price-sensitive SMB') is contradicted by its own source record exp_73, which shows a 31% signup lift but a 12% 30-day retention drop, meaning the acquired cohort churns before renewal — explicitly flagged as non-sustainable. Given the objective is long-term qualified revenue, matching the competitor's price cut would likely repeat this failure mode, so promotional_pricing is deliberately avoided despite competitive pressure. In contrast, exp_31 confirms signup simplification durably improves SMB activation with negligible retention cost (-1%) and positive revenue (+4%), and memory_86 corroborates onboarding shortening's positive effect on adoption. This gives a verified, sustainable lever to address the price-sensitive SMB churn conversations without the retention risk seen in discounting. Scale is kept at standard_experiment rather than broad_rollout because current market conditions (aggressive competitor pricing) differ from when exp_31 was validated, so re-confirming impact under this new pressure is prudent before full rollout. Verification budget is spent, so no new archive pulls are used; decision rests on already-recovered source data.
